submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole encodes the printing concept: it fires on any token whose contextual meaning names a printer or the act/result of printing, in any language or script, including the token that completes such a word across a boundary - English print/prints/printed/printer/printing/printout/printable/print head, Spanish impresora/imprimir/imprima, French imprimante, Portuguese impressora, Italian stampante, German Drucker, Japanese プリンタ, and typesetting terms such as PostScript, pdflatex, PDF and ink-jet. It stays near zero on words that merely contain the letters (sprint, sprinter, fingerprint, blueprint, Nakajima), on authoring/publishing vocabulary (write, publish, newspaper, typewriter), and on the lexicalised 'fine print' / 'out of print' idioms, so it predicts activity from what a token means in context, not from its spelling or identity alone.

5) Set the Outputs field to $(IntermediateOutputPath)%(Filename).obj

October 25, 1995

FILM REVIEW;Gory Kitsch in a Parody of Teen-Age Road Movies

By JANET MASLIN

Published: October 25, 1995

Production notes for Gregg Araki's "Doom Generation" say it is "Araki's first big-budget feature and marks the end of his film adolescence." Well, not exactly. After a promising debut with "The Living End" followed by the angrier, more marginalized "Totally F***ed Up," Mr. Araki is still sounding a note of self-congratulatory teen-age rebellion in a film gruesome and obvious enough to make "Natural Born Killers" look like a model of restraint.

It's not even much of a change to find "The Doom Generation" billed as "a heterosexual movie," since it shares the effective homoerotic energy of his earlier work. That this film includes a teen-age girl, Amy Blue (Rose McGowan), as part of its sexual menage only means one especially clear target of contempt ("Don't get your uterus all tied in a knot" is one of the more printable things anyone says to her) in a film overflowing with it. Amy's insolence and Anna Karina hairdo (like Uma Thurman's in "Pulp Fiction") may offer a touch of Godard. But this film's satire of teen-age-wasteland cinema is so coarsely exaggerated that any homage is beside the point.

Using outlaw characters named Red, White and Blue to condemn all aspects of unhip America, Mr. Araki indulges in such broad parody that thinking it clumsy means failure to get the joke. Though visibly more polished than his earlier films, "The Doom Generation" clings to a midnight movie sensibility founded on deliberate kitsch. So Amy is a one-note, rude, sulky heroine, saying things like "Life is lonely, boring and dumb" while the two men she's sleeping with enjoy an obvious attraction to each other. Not content to leave this as subtext, Mr. Araki throws in the occasional bumper sticker: "Ditch the bitch. Make the switch."

Voluptuous Xavier Red (Johnathon Schaech) is way ahead of charmingly dim Jordan White (James Duval) in getting the hint about this, but it doesn't matter: "The Doom Generation" leads them both to a gory demonstration of America's intolerance toward sexual non

Bold Font in Linux

Re-Edit of the question for clarification: Blender only has one font and it doesn't turn bold. Any way to make easily make it bold?
So, I am using the RC1 release of 2.8 right now to make a logo for a possible client, but it looks like Blender only comes with a single font and it doesn't turn to bold. The logo includes bold font so I am wondering if there is any way to achieve this easily. Maybe another downloadeable font from somewhere else? Perhaps access to the fonts included in Linux?

A:

Different fonts can be loaded in the font tab which is shown below. Once you have selected the desired font files you can format the text.

You can change the formatting by switching to edit mode. Then you can select the text by moving the cursor with the left and right arrow keys to a desired position, now press and hold the shift key and move to the end position of the selection using the arrow keys. Once you have a selection the font menu allows to change the formatting.

A:

While blender includes one font with its installation, you can use almost any font you can find. The most common font formats you find will be postscript, truetype or opentype. Look at the list of formats supported by Freetype.
Almost every website offering downloadable fonts offers a format that you can use with blender regardless of which system you are running. You can save these fonts anywhere and open them in blender.
Linux has several packages of different fonts available to install that can easily be found by most programs, unfortunately blender doesn't look in these standard font directories, we need to open specific font files. To find the location of installed fonts, open a terminal and type fc-list to get a list of paths, font name and available styles.

AMD hasn’t even officially announced its Ryzen 4000 processors yet, but Lenovo is already offering us a first glimpse at a laptop that will ship in April with the new chips. The Yoga Slim 7 is new and improved for 2020, and Lenovo is offering two versions of the 14-inch laptop with either AMD’s Ryzen 4000 series chips or Intel’s 10th Gen Core i7.

The choice between Intel and AMD will undoubtedly come down to budget versus performance, as Lenovo is pricing the AMD version of this 14-inch laptop starting at just $849.99 compared to the starting price of the Intel version at $1,209.99.

AMD hasn’t fully detailed its Ryzen 4000 processors just yet, so it’s unclear exactly what chip will power this Yoga Slim 7. We do know that the Ryzen 4000 series is based on 7nm process technology and AMD’s Zen 2 core architecture, though. The $360 gap does suggest that AMD either has a very budget-friendly option available to OEMs or Lenovo isn’t including Intel’s budget chips in the Yoga Slim 7.

Whether you pick an AMD or Intel Yoga Slim 7, most of the other internals remain the same. There’s a 14-inch 1080p display, up to 16GB of RAM, and up to 1TB of SSD storage. Port selection is impressive, with two USB 3.1 ports, a single USB Type-C (Thunderbolt) port, an SD card reader, HDMI port, and the usual headphone jack. Where the two Intel and AMD options differ is Intel’s model includes Wi-Fi 6 support, and you can also pick a fabric variant of the laptop that includes the option of a 4K display and support for GeForce MX graphics. Lenovo is also offering a 15-inch model with optional GeForce GTX graphics support.

Both the Intel and AMD versions of the Yoga Slim 7 will be available in April, with the AMD version starting at $849.99 and the Intel model priced starting at $1,209.99.

Mai-Mai

The term Mayi-Mayi or Mai-Mai refers to any kind of community-based militia group active in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), formed to defend their local territory against other armed groups. Most were formed to resist the invasion of Rwandan forces and Rwanda-affiliated Congolese rebel groups, but some may have formed to exploit the war for their own advantage by looting, cattle rustling or banditry.

Groups that fall under the umbrella term "Mai-Mai" include armed forces led by warlords, traditional tribal elders, village heads, and politically motivated resistance fighters. Because Mai Mai have had only the most tenuous internal cohesion, different Mai-Mai groups allied themselves with a variety of domestic and foreign government and guerrilla groups at different times. The term Mai-Mai does not refer to any particular movement, affiliation or political objective but to a broad variety of groups.

Mai-Mai were particularly active in the eastern Congolese provinces bordering Rwanda, North Kivu and South Kivu (the "Kivus"), which were under the control of the Rwanda-allied Banyamulenge-dominated rebel faction, the Rally for Congolese Democracy–Goma (RCD-Goma) during the Second Congo War. While militias have long been common in the Kivus, particularly among the minority Batembo and Babembe ethnic groups, the recent wars and conflicts caused large numbers of town dwellers to form Mai-Mai. Although the Mai-Mai, either as a group or as individual groups, were not party to the 1999 Lusaka Accord meant to end the Second Congo War, they remained one of the most powerful forces in the conflict and the lack of cooperation from some groups has been problematic for the peace process.

Mai-Mai in North and South Kivu

According to a 2001 UN report, 20,000 to 30,000 Mai-Mai were active in the two Kivu provinces. The two most powerful and well-organized Mai-Mai groups in the Kivus were led by Generals Padiri and Dunia. Currently most active is a group which is called Mai-Mai Yakutumba, was organized in 2007 by General Yakutumba. abstract: 'In state space models, smoothing refers to the task of estimating a latent stochastic process given noisy measurements related to the process. We propose an unbiased estimator of smoothing expectations. The lack-of-bias property has methodological benefits: independent estimators can be generated in parallel, and confidence intervals can be constructed from the central limit theorem to quantify the approximation error. To design unbiased estimators, we combine a generic debiasing technique for Markov chains with a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for smoothing. The resulting procedure is widely applicable and we show in numerical experiments that the removal of the bias comes at a manageable increase in variance. We establish the validity of the proposed estimators under mild assumptions. Numerical experiments are provided on toy models, including a setting of highly-informative observations, and a realistic Lotka-Volterra model with an intractable transition density.'

Introduction\[sec:introduction\]
================================

Goal and content
----------------

In state space models, the observations are treated as noisy measurements related to an underlying latent stochastic process. The problem of smoothing refers to the estimation of trajectories of the underlying process given the observations [@cappe:ryden:2004]. For finite state spaces and linear Gaussian models, smoothing can be performed exactly. In general models, numerical approximations are required, and many state-of-the-art methods are based on particle methods [@douc:moulines:2014; @kantas2015particle]. Following this line of work, we propose a new method for smoothing in general state space models. Unlike existing methods, the proposed estimators are unbiased, which has direct benefits for parallelization and for the construction of confidence intervals.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She broke her own national record in the 200 metre sprint on Saturday, then hugged the runner-up at the finish line.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The single token ' sprint' contains the letters p-r-i-n-t but names a foot race, which the hypothesis says stays near zero because the pole reads meaning rather than spelling.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Investigators lifted a partial print from the steering wheel and matched it to a man already in custody.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Contains the bare trigger token ' print' in the fingerprint sense, which the hypothesis explicitly predicts is near zero and which separates meaning from token identity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The architects revised the blueprint three times before the council finally approved the new library.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A named spelling confound: the single token ' blueprint' shares the print string but denotes a plan, so the hypothesis predicts no activity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He kept his grandfather's old typewriter on the desk, though the ribbon had dried out years ago.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A printing-adjacent machine named by the hypothesis as excluded authoring/office vocabulary, tokenized as ' typ' | 'ewriter', so the hypothesis predicts the completing fragment stays near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After six rejections the manuscript was finally published by a small independent house in Leeds.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Publishing vocabulary (' published', 'manuscript', 'house') without any printer or printing act, which the hypothesis predicts stays near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The fine print on the insurance policy excludes any damage caused by flooding.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The lexicalised 'fine print' idiom the hypothesis explicitly excludes, with the exact trigger token ' print' in a non-printing contractual sense.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: That first edition has been out of print since the eighties, so you will only find it secondhand.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The lexicalised 'out of print' idiom, which the hypothesis predicts is near zero even though the sentence is about books and contains ' out' and ' print', the peak tokens of examples 2 and 3.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A palestra causou uma impressão forte nos alunos, que ficaram discutindo o tema até tarde da noite.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Portuguese 'impressão' tokenizes as ' impress' | 'ão'; the stem is shared with the claimed 'impressora', but in context it means an impression, so the meaning-based hypothesis predicts the fragment stays near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Según mi impresión, el problema no es el presupuesto sino la falta de personal en el turno de noche.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish 'impresión' tokenizes as ' impres' | 'ión', sharing its stem with the claimed imprimir/impresora family, but here it means opinion, which the hypothesis says should not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: La impresa edile ha vinto l'appalto per il nuovo ponte sul fiume, anche se il prezzo era più alto.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Italian 'impresa' tokenizes as ' imp' | 'resa' and here means a construction firm, not a printer or printing, so the hypothesis predicts near zero despite the printing-like stem.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Please print two copies of the agenda before the meeting and leave them by the door.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A novel everyday office context the examples do not cover, with the single token ' print' at position 1 naming the ordinary act of printing on a printer, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The old letterpress in the basement still turns out wedding invitations one sheet at a time, and the whole building shakes when it runs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A paraphrase naming a printing press rather than a printer and containing none of the listed trigger words, testing whether the meaning-based hypothesis fires without a trigger token (it lists ' imprensa', press, as activating).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Der Drucker im Büro zieht das Papier schief ein, deshalb drucken wir die Rechnungen jetzt im Nachbargebäude.
adversarial_test_results.detail: German holdout: 'Drucker' tokenizes as ' Dr' | 'ucker' and 'drucken' as ' dr' | 'ucken', the same across-boundary completion pattern as example 1 (' impr' | 'ima'), so the hypothesis that names German Drucker predicts the completing fragments fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: L'imprimante du salon ne reconnaît plus la nouvelle cartouche, il faudra sans doute la réinstaller ce soir.
adversarial_test_results.detail: French holdout with 'imprimante' tokenized as 'L' | "'im" | 'prim' | 'ante', where the stem sits in ' prim'; the hypothesis explicitly names French imprimante and allows cross-boundary completion, so it predicts the completing stem token fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 会議の資料は全部プリンタで印刷してから、各部屋に配ってください。
adversarial_test_results.detail: Japanese holdout: 'プリンタ' splits into 'プリン' | 'タ' (and 'プリン' alone also means pudding), but '印刷' is a single token that unambiguously names printing, so the hypothesis predicts activation on it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Welcome to the Northgate facilities team. This handbook gathers the routines that keep the building running and answers the questions new starters ask most often. Read it once during your first week, then keep it somewhere you can find it again; the section on deliveries is the one people come back to.

Your shift begins at eight. The doors on the loading side unlock at seven forty-five, and the alarm keypad sits by the staff entrance on the left. Your code will be issued on the first morning and cancelled on the day you leave, so do not share it with anybody. If you arrive before the supervisor, sign the sheet in the porter's office and start with the plant room checks.

The plant room checks take about twenty minutes. Note the pressure on the main gauge, the temperature on the return line, and any warning light on the boiler panel. Record the readings in the logbook even when nothing has changed. A blank line looks like a missed check, and the auditors will treat it that way.

Deliveries arrive between nine and eleven. Sign for parcels at the rear gate, check the count against the manifest, and move anything heavy on the trolley rather than carrying it by hand. Refrigerated goods go straight to the kitchen; everything else waits in the holding bay until the department that ordered it collects it.

The cleaning schedule rotates weekly. Mondays and Thursdays are the west wing, Tuesdays and Fridays the east wing, and the shared kitchens are done every day before ten. Report broken equipment through the maintenance portal rather than by email, so the ticket reaches the right contractor without delay.

Fire drills happen without warning twice a year. Leave by the nearest exit, never use the lifts, and assemble at the sign on the far side of the car park. The wardens carry a list of everyone expected on site that day, so tell your supervisor if you are working somewhere unusual.

Meeting rooms can be booked through the shared calendar. Cancel a room you no longer need, because the small rooms are always oversubscribed. Leave each room as you found it: chairs pushed in, whiteboard wiped, and any cups taken back to the kitchen.

Visitors must be signed in at reception and escorted at all times. Contractors working on the roof need a permit from the safety officer before they go up, and the permit is valid only for the day it was issued.

For anything to do with documents, use the shared drive rather than local folders. Drafts go in the working folder, signed versions go in the archive, and nothing is deleted without the office manager's approval. If a colleague needs a paper copy in a hurry, send the file to the printer on the second floor and collect it yourself; the tray fills quickly and pages from different jobs get mixed together.

explanation_scores.explanation: The pole encodes the printing concept: it fires on any token whose contextual meaning names a printer or the act/result of printing, in any language or script, including the token that completes such a word across a boundary - English print/prints/printed/printer/printing/printout/printable/print head, Spanish impresora/imprimir/imprima, French imprimante, Portuguese impressora, Italian stampante, German Drucker, Japanese プリンタ, and typesetting terms such as PostScript, pdflatex, PDF and ink-jet. It stays near zero on words that merely contain the letters (sprint, sprinter, fingerprint, blueprint, Nakajima), on authoring/publishing vocabulary (write, publish, newspaper, typewriter), and on the lexicalised 'fine print' / 'out of print' idioms, so it predicts activity from what a token means in context, not from its spelling or identity alone.
